correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact nonlinear duality identity at every two-coordinate input, pairwise disjointness of nonzero columns follows from the dominating fractional power for 1<p<2 or from a nonnegative real Hessian with zero kernel only off the support for p>2. The row/column identity at each basis vector makes all active columns monomial and forces a support involution; a mixture of zero and nonzero columns is impossible; comparison of mixed input coefficients makes all nonzero weights equal in modulus. The conjugate weight condition yields a direct converse. Thus every nonzero solution squares to a positive scalar identity, proving the infinite-dimensional compactness corollary. A Python standard-library checker tests 480 constructive and 960 excluded examples but is not treated as proof.

value.rationale: This is a full structural classification for a natural non-Hilbert operator property and all dimensions and index sets, not a routine identity. It collapses a potentially vast operator class to scaled isometric involutions; forces an exact quadratic functional calculus and excludes nonzero compact solutions on infinite-dimensional non-Hilbert ell_p, revealing a sharp Hilbert/non-Hilbert boundary of the contemporary compact spectral theory.
